component.name: Lurker
component.summary: Watch Twitch channels with their chat

description.p: A native desktop client for watching Twitch. Streams play through mpv, without ads, alongside a chat with 7TV, BTTV and FFZ emotes.

ul.li: Browse followed channels, top streams and categories
Open other channels' chats as splits beside the video
Chat with history, reply threads, highlights and moderator tools
Watch past broadcasts with seeking and chat replay
Choose the quality, or switch to low latency
See stream stats, including latency to the broadcaster
Get a notification when a channel you follow goes live

description.p: Lurker is not affiliated with or endorsed by Twitch.

screenshot.caption: A live stream with its chat

description.p: Lurker has its own Flatpak repository: install it once from sp1r17.github.io/lurker and flatpak update or your software center keeps it up to date, and the release's Flatpak file now gets updates from it too. Lurker quits when the compositor or X server goes away, instead of running on unseen with the stream still playing. On Wayland, dragging the window by the video or header keeps working after the mouse is disconnected and connected again, or when Lurker started without one.

Watching past broadcasts no longer uses more and more memory: the seek bar's preview images were never freed, so scrubbing through videos could take Lurker past a gigabyte and a half. When something doesn't load from Twitch, Lurker now says why, telling a change to Twitch's API apart from Twitch being unreachable, and the offline channels you follow, your own emotes, videos opened from History and chat replay say so too instead of showing nothing. Settings has a Bug reports section that copies Lurker's log, including the run before for when it crashed, and opens the log folder. Live notifications are no longer offered on macOS, where they'd need an app signed by Apple.

The quality menu lists each stream's own qualities, such as 936p, and a highest quality can be set. Press I for stream stats: resolution, bitrate, network speed, buffer, dropped frames, ping to Twitch and latency to the broadcaster. Chat can be delayed to match the stream, and low latency can keep a small buffer. Live cards show uptime; stream lists can be sorted; a History tab lists what you've watched; the start page can be chosen; and clips can be limited to the last day, week or month. Right-click a card to follow its channel or category, mute its notifications or copy its link, or choose to be notified only for some channels. Chat can show timestamps, highlight the streamer and moderators, hide bots and alternate backgrounds. R restarts a stuck stream, a Live now button appears on a live channel's older videos, and the next clip plays when one ends. Still-live broadcasts show the stream's current frame, and the screenshots are new.

Clicking the "More messages below" bar over a name now jumps to the newest messages instead of opening that person's card, and emotes under the bar no longer show their tooltip. Lurker now also runs on Macs with Apple silicon.

A Settings page, from the link at the top or Ctrl+comma, gathers notifications, update checks, text size, low latency, following raids, the primary language, chat highlights and ignored users, what's blocked, and signing out. Double-clicking the video now maximizes the window like the maximize button; F goes fullscreen. Saved settings record their format and are written safely, so a crash can't corrupt them. Lurker is now licensed under the GPL, version 3 or later.

Pin a user card to keep it open while you click around the chat. A new emote button beside the chat box lists every emote you can send, with a search box; click one to put it in your message. Large 7TV emote sets load several times faster.
A live stream that goes offline and comes back reloads by itself. Fixes the window freezing when the audio output hung, on Linux.

Block channels and categories to hide them everywhere: right-click a card, or open Blocked at the top. Pick a primary language, and streams in other languages are grayed out or hidden. When the channel you're watching raids another, Lurker follows the raid.

Fixes for Windows: the video's controls show when the mouse is over a stream, dragging the video moves the window, and chat badges and emotes load. Badges also show on chat messages that arrived before they loaded.
Lurker tells you when a new version is out, with a switch at the top of the browse screen to turn that off. Top no longer shows the last opened category's streams.

Streams in 1440p, and the quality menu only lists the qualities a stream has. Chat shows recent messages on joining, clickable links, reply threads and the chat's modes, with your own highlight phrases and ignored users. User cards list everything someone said, and moderators can time out, ban and delete messages.

A desktop notification when a channel you follow goes live, while Lurker is open, with the channel's picture. Click it to watch the stream. Notifications can be turned off at the top of the browse screen.
Fixes memory use that kept growing while a video played (about 1 GB an hour on NVIDIA).
A Videos button in the bar above the stream, to reach a channel's videos while it's live.

ul.li: Each channel's past broadcasts, highlights, uploads and clips, with chat replay
Resume videos where you left off
Watch a live stream from its start
Playback speed, chapters and seek-bar previews
Open Twitch video and clip links
